* 4. reconcile-once!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/reconcile-once!
:FILE: src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj
:LINE: 675
:MINS: 3.7
:END:

One reconcile pass: read enabled rows, apply ~diff-desired~, detect config drift, and race advisory-lock slots. This is BOTH the edge-triggered handler (fired by ~:service~ CRUD / NOTIFY) and the level-triggered periodic tick — the placeholder it recomputes each pass is exactly what heals a crashed lock-owner on the next tick.

The supervisor that actually keeps a fn running: invoke the target fn via the executor and, on a startup failure, sleep + retry up to N times per the row's ~:restart-policy~, stamping ~:start-failed-at~ when exhausted so reconcile will not busy-loop. The ~how a service stays up~ answer that closes out the services half.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj::(defn start-service!][src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj:161]]

* 6. endpoint-of
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/endpoint-of
:FILE: src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj
:LINE: 261
:MINS: 1.3
:END:

A service that listens somewhere ANSWERS somewhere: the handle ~:http-server~ returns carries ~{:endpoint {:port p}}~ as metadata, and the pod that started it completes that with its own dialable host (the fleet ~:executor-id~, or loopback) before writing this copy's ~:service-instance~ row — host, port, and a heartbeat it refreshes every tick. Read this next because it is the write side of service-to-service — the fact every consumer resolves.

:PROPERTIES:

:LINE: 125
:MINS: 3.4

The write-time cycle check's closure, since a consumer named the editor's own listener: the ref's execution graph is loaded through ~sp/resolve-execution-graph~ (one recursive CTE) and walked in memory — the edges ~forward-deps-of~ follows, identity edges skipped, constraint-vector type names resolved per round. No per-fn queries, no visit cap; the old walk took seconds and then refused as ~chain-too-deep~.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/protocol/generic_constraints.clj::(defn dependency-closure][src/graphden/storage/protocol/generic_constraints.clj:125]]

* 8. check-liveness!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/check-liveness!
:FILE: src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj
:LINE: 457
:MINS: 2.5
:END:

The per-tick liveness pass: a handle may also carry ~:alive?~ and ~:exit~ (http-kit's listener status; a ~:future~'s thread state and how it ended), so a copy that died IN PLACE is caught here — its row deleted, its lock released — and the row's ~:restart-policy~ finally means what it says: ~:always~ restarts any exit, ~:on-failure~ only a throw, ~:never~ parks it. Live copies just get their heartbeat.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj::(defn- check-liveness!][src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj:457]]

* 9. resolve-endpoint
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/resolve-endpoint
:FILE: src/graphden/services/endpoint.clj
:LINE: 86
:MINS: 2.0
:END:

The read side: a consumer names a service through a ~:fn-ref~ slot (~:service-endpoint :service :orders-service~ — the fn's identity, never evaluated, not a dependency, so two services may name each other) and this turns the id into ~{:host :port :url}~ — a LIVE instance (fresh heartbeat, this pod's copy first) of the fn's row on the caller's branch, else the addon-installed ~resolver~ (a cloud app-route's public origin), else an honest ~:service/not-running~. The web/service templates (~:service-get~) compose it with http-client; nothing here dials.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/services/endpoint.clj::(defn resolve-endpoint][src/graphden/services/endpoint.clj:86]]

* 10. run-traced!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/run-traced!
:FILE: src/graphden/crud/fn_execution/trace.clj
:LINE: 103
:MINS: 1.7
:END:

A call across the wire stays one tree: a persisted run's ~:service-get~ sends ~X-Graphden-Trace~ (trace id + its own execution id), and the listener runs the request through this — a fresh execution id bound for the handler's own outbound calls, a path trace, and the outcome persisted as an execution of the handler fn linked to the caller. No header, no row: ordinary traffic pays nothing. ~get-execution~ then lists a run's ~:children~.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/crud/fn_execution/trace.clj::(defn run-traced!][src/graphden/crud/fn_execution/trace.clj:103]]

The other way two services talk: a queue. One Postgres table with the standard job-queue shape — ~pending~/~dead~, attempts, a due time, a visibility lock — that ~storage/queue~'s four primitives drive (~FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED~ for the claim, NOTIFY to wake a waiting taker). The consumer LOOP is graph composition in that module's fns.edn, with the backend as fn-typed slots — read this to see why a broker was not needed.

* 15. pack
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/pack
:FILE: src/graphden/fleet/packer.clj
:LINE: 69
:MINS: 2.7
:END:

The LPT (longest-processing-time-first) greedy packer: sort cells heaviest-first and drop each on the least-loaded executor — the classic makespan 2-approximation. It answers ~what SHOULD the placement be~ for a from-scratch layout.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/fleet/packer.clj::(defn pack][src/graphden/fleet/packer.clj:69]]

* 16. rebalance
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/rebalance
:FILE: src/graphden/fleet/rebalance.clj
:LINE: 81
:MINS: 5.0
:END:

The churn-minimising planner: rather than diff against a fresh pack, do steepest-descent (move one cell busiest → lightest while it strictly reduces spread) with a ~:min-improvement~ hysteresis floor, emitting the FEWEST moves. How a running fleet is nudged toward balance without thrashing.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/fleet/rebalance.clj::(defn rebalance][src/graphden/fleet/rebalance.clj:81]]

:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/plan-tick

The pure brain of one control pass: always emit initial placements for unheld cells, but gate rebalance moves behind ~:sustain-ticks~ so imbalance must PERSIST (not just spike) before cells move. Composes the packer + rebalancer into the actual control policy.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/fleet/control_loop.clj::(defn plan-tick][src/graphden/fleet/control_loop.clj:63]]
